notes.raw:
\*Data above 298 K estimated except temperature and enthalpy of fusion. 
Phase changes: 544.59 K, melting point of Bi; $\Delta H^{\circ} = 2.700$ kcal/mol. 
1036 K, melting point of $Bi_{2}S_{3}$ ; $\Delta H^{\circ} = 18.970$ kcal/mol. 
Heat capacity (cal/mol·K) and enthalpy (kcal/mol) equations: 
298.15-1036 K: $Cp^{0} = 29.620 + 5.344 \times 10^{-3} T - 1.815 \times 10^{5} T^{-2}$ 
$H^{0}-H_{298}^{0}=29.620\times10^{-3}T+2.672\times10^{-6}T^{2}+1.815\times10^{2}T^{-1}-9.677$ 
1036-1200 K: $Cp^{\circ} = 50.000$ 
$H^{\circ}-H_{298}^{\circ}=50.000\times10^{-3}T-8.778$ 
Reaction equations (kcal/mol): 
298.15-544.59 K: $\Delta \mathrm{Hr}^{\circ} = -92.591 + 10.459 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} - 4.212 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 233.250 \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ 
$\Delta Gr^{\circ} = -92.591 - 10.459 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} + 4.212 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 116.625 \mathrm{T}^{-1} + 129.833 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
544.59-1036 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = -98.145 + 5.399 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} + 1.874 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 834.450 \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ 
$\Delta Gr^{\circ} = -98.145 - 5.399 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} - 1.874 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 417.225 \mathrm{T}^{-1} + 110.453 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
1036-1200 K: $\Delta \mathrm{Hr}^{\circ} = -97.245 + 25.779 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} - 0.798 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 652.950 \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ 
$\Delta \mathrm{Gr}^{\circ} = -97.245 - 25.779 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} + 0.798 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 326.475 \mathrm{T}^{-1} + 248.402 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
Sources: Enthalpy of formation at 298 K based on Prusaczyk (101) and Mitchell (81). Low-temperature heat capacities and entropy at 298 K from Romanovskii (102). Fusion data from Glatz (44). All other data estimated.
